description: §6.8.4 rule 1 on a pending cell (§13.9.2): `reset-on=[@tick]` performs `reset(@self)` when `@tick` changes, and a reset of a pending cell is its load's re-run. The locked cell reads no cell, so without the rule it would load once ("a"); the handler renames the row on the server and then writes `@tick`, which re-runs the load and settles the new name ("z"). RUNTIME, sqlEngine "real".
rationale: §6.8.4 rule 1: "When any listed cell changes … the runtime SHALL perform `reset(@self)`". §13.9.2: "A reset of a pending cell (§6.8) is the request's re-run." §13.9.1 S475 rule 5: "The compiler-written load writes are exempt from grant checks." ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S447 "3b: `reset-on=` IS allowed on engine cells" (the modifier) and S475 "⭐ RULED — S475 owner questions" item 1 (the pending-cell spelling).
